English: African marigold (Tagetes erecta) – mbangimwitu. Use against: bacteria, fungi, nematodes, insects (ants, beetles and many others). Preparation: crush 100-200g of the leaves, roots or flowers, pour on 1 litre of boiling water, stir, and soak for 24 hours, then add 1 litre of cold water. Spray on plants or into the soil.
Kiswahili: African marigold / Mbangimwitu (Tagetes erecta). Inazuia: bacteria, fungi, nematodes, wadudu (ants, beetles na wadudu wengine wengi). Kutayarisha: ponda gramu 100-200 ya matawi, mizizi na maua; mwaga kwa lita moja ya maji yaliyochemka; lowa kwa masaa ishirini na nne; ongeza lita moja ya maji baridi; nyunyiza kwa mimea au mchanga.

English: Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) – kiazi kitamu. Use against: rice brown leaf spot, rice blast and other fungal diseases, insects (aphids). Preparation: crush and soak leaves in water, use as spray. Heavily starched water after cooking can be sprayed on small insects such as aphids.
Kiswahili: Sweet Potato / Kiazi kitamu (Ipomea batatas). Inazuia: rice brown leaf spot, rice blast na magonjwa mengine ya ukungu, wadudu (aphids). Kutayarisha: ponda na ulowe majani kwa maji, nyunyiza. Maji yanayo wanga mzito baada ya kupika yanaweza kunyunyizwa kwa wadudu wadogo kama aphids.

English: Tea (Camellia sinensis) – chai. Use against: fungal diseases, insects, snails (woolly aphid, squash bug, termite mounds). Preparation: the used leaves can be spread around plants to repel snails. The liquid (tea), when cool, can be sprayed on plants.
Kiswahili: Tea / Chai (Camellia sinensis). Inazuia: magonjwa ya ukungu, wadudu, konokono (wooly aphid, squash bug, mchwa). Kutayarisha: matawi ambayo yametumika yaweza kutawanywa karibu na mimea kufukuza dudu makamasi (konokono). Maji baridi yaweza kunyunyiziwa kwa mimea.

English: When crops are damaged during or after harvest, they quickly spoil. You may not be able to sell your damaged produce, or you may be forced to sell at a reduced price. On the other hand, if you can reduce your losses, you can increase your income. At harvest time, when picking fruits, be careful not to knock them off the tree and onto the ground. If fruit falls, it gets bruised, disease and insects attack, and the fruit will quickly spoil. If you reduce the number of falls, you will have high quality produce to sell.
Kiswahili: Mazao yanapojeruhiwa wakati wa kuvuna au mara baada ya mavuno, yanaharibika kwa haraka. Unaweza kushindwa kuuza mazao yaliyoharibika au kujeruhiwa, na wakati mwingine ukalazimika kuyauza kwa bei ndogo. Kwa upande mwingine, kama utafanikiwa kupunguza hasara, unaweza pia kuongeza kipato chako. Wakati wa mavuno, unapokuwa ukichuma matunda, kuwa mwangalifu, usiyagonge kwenye mti au kuyaacha yakaanguka ardhini. Kama tunda likianguka chini, linaweza kupata michubuko, magonjwa na vijidudu vinalishambulia, na tunda huharibika. Kama utaweza kuzuia idadi ya matunda yanayoanguka chini, utakuwa na bidhaa bora sokoni.

English: When crops are damaged during or after harvest, they quickly spoil, so you may be forced to sell at a reduced price. The best time to harvest fruits and vegetables is in the morning — wait until the dew has evaporated, then harvest before the day gets too hot. Harvesting later in the day leaves fruits and vegetables wilted or limp, with more disease and insect problems. Harvest in the morning for firmer, fresher produce.
Kiswahili: Matunda yanapokuwa yamejeruhiwa wakati wa kuvuna ama baada ya kuvuna, huharibika kwa haraka, hivyo unaweza kulazimika kuyauza kwa bei ya chini. Muda mzuri wa kuvuna matunda na mboga ni asubuhi — subiri mpaka umande umekauka, halafu vuna kabla jua halijawa kali. Ukivuna wakati wa jua kali, matunda na mboga zinaweza kusinyaa au kunyauka, na kushambuliwa zaidi na magonjwa au wadudu. Vuna asubuhi ili upate mazao mazuri na imara.
